newsitem.title: DENMARK: Dutch Gasunie plans gas pipeline to Britain.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Gasunie plans gas pipeline to Britain.

text.p: COPENHAGEN, June 11, Reuter - Dutch gas giant Gasunie is planning a gas pipeline from the Netherlands to the east coast of England, Gasunie head of business development Willem Mensink told Reuters on Wednesday.
The pipeline would run from Den Helder in the Netherlands to Britain's Bacton terminal and initially could provide extra supplies to the U.K. during peak winter demand.
"We are planning a line to Bacton," said Mensink. "Very soon the U.K. will need capacity in winter, and we see a good possibility to deliver that capacity."
"We're now involved in a study and talking with parties in the U.K. If they want to buy capacity from us we'll build it," Mensink added

Gasunie believed that in the future the U.K., despite its own large North Sea reserves, would become a net importer of gas, Mensink said. "It may be after 10 years, maybe longer, but it will have to import large volumes," he said.
He added that if the pipeline was built, it could be to import gas from Britain in the first instance.
But in that case, Gasunie would leave its imports at Bacton during the winter, so they were on hand to be sold back into the U.K. during the winter peak.

The Interconnector pipeline from Bacton to Zeebrugge in Belgium is already under construction and will be operating by October 1998. Several deals have alrady been signed for delivery of gas to European customers, including one to a subsidiary of Norsk Hydro NHY.ST in the Netherlands.
Gasunie has been more resistant than many European gas companies to the liberalisation of markets proposed by the EU and enthusiastically carried out in Britain.

"We say no to liberalisation," said Mensink, although he said that Gasunie's transport system has always been open to third party access to customers prepared to pay for it. But so far few have done so.

"In the last few years we have been almost the only ones to sell gas in the Netherlands," he said, although a power station in the North of the country has a deal to buy gas from Norway and transorts it a short way through the Gasunie system.
He added that Energie Zuid Nederlands is looking to build its own pipeline in the south west of the country, and the Norsk Hydro subsidiary buys direct from Mobil Corp's MEGAS (Mobil Europe Gas Inc).

Mensink believed it inevitable that an EU gas directive would be signed, and that Gasunie will lose market share, although he said that the company would compete on price - unlike the U.K.'s British Gas which was explicitly prevented from doing so - to keep customers. But the company will not enter a damaging price war.

"We think we will lose more because others will offer a lower price," Mensink said. "But we will not sell against a price that's lower than the cost we have to make. If we see what's happening now, some parties are offering lower prices."

Gasunie has entered a deal with Russia's Gazprom under which Gasunie buys gas and delivers services in return, which could include storing gas for Gazprom to deliver to potential customers in western Europe.

"We have a deal with Gazprom because they have huge reserves and will be the main supplier in the long term. And we think we can make money by selling services," he said. But he added there are no plans to enter similar arrangements with any other companies.
Gasunie sold 93.8 billion cubic metres (bcm) of gas in 1996, up nearly 13 percent from 83.1 bcm in 1995. Of this 45.9 bcm was exported, up 19.5 percent from 1995's figure of38.4 bcm.
